title: An Enhanced Primary and Secondary Control for Voltage Regulation in an Islanded DC Microgrid
content: Voltage regulation is a critical control objective in islanded DC microgrids to ensure stable and reliable system operation. Hierarchical control provides a structured approach to maintaining DC bus voltage through coordinated primary and secondary control layers. However, conventional control strategies based on fixed droop characteristics and conventional secondary voltage restoration may exhibit limitations under varying operating conditions and sudden load disturbances. To address these limitations, this paper proposes an enhanced primary and secondary control strategy for voltage regulation in an islanded DC microgrid. At the primary level, an adaptive droop control technique is employed to improve DC bus voltage response under varying operating conditions. At the secondary level, an adaptive centralized voltage restoration controller is developed to compensate for voltage deviations introduced by primary droop control and maintain the DC bus voltage close to its nominal reference value. The proposed control strategy is implemented and evaluated using MATLAB/Simulink. Its performance is compared with conventional hierarchical control under steady-state, load-increase, and load-decrease operating conditions. The comparative analysis considers DC bus voltage deviation, minimum voltage, and final voltage regulation. Simulation results demonstrate an approximately 59\% reduction in steady-state voltage deviation and improved final voltage regulation during load decrease. However, the transient response remains comparable to conventional control. The results indicate that the proposed strategy improves steady-state voltage regulation and final voltage recovery in the considered islanded DC microgrid.
